meta.title: Serbian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 88 expressions · 35 everyday, 37 idioms, 16 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 88 Serbian set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 35 everyday phrases, 37 idioms and 16 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Serbian → English (see the Serbian, recall the meaning) and English → Serbian (see an English meaning, recall the Serbian) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the five level decks, Serbian A1 to C1, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the five, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Serbian speaker uses as one piece (kako si, koliko dugo, kako ste …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (babe i žabe, gurnuti pod tepih, čitati između redova …), and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (ljubav je slepa, mi o vuku a vuk na vrata, bolje vrabac u ruci nego golub na grani …). Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Serbian sentences contain them, an expression with a verb being counted in any form of that verb; only 25 of the 88 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how common their words are in film and television subtitles. The Serbian is the Ekavian standard of Serbia, and expressions Wiktionary marks as only Croatian or Bosnian are left out. Every expression is printed in Cyrillic with its accent marked as Wiktionary gives it, and again in the Latin alphabet beneath. Real example sentences come with 23 of the 88 expressions, three apiece for 4, in Cyrillic with the Latin beneath, the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, accents and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
